channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: A.I. Hurricane Models Were Front and Center as Isaias Headed Toward Land
item.description: Expert forecasters say the new technology is helping them understand where a storm will go.

item.title: NPR: Opinion: Can I keep the baseball I caught?
item.description: What would you do if you caught a baseball during the MLB playoffs? Give it to a kid nearby or keep it? This very scenario played out this week, with a fan deciding to keep the ball.

item.title: BBC News: Christa Pike discharged from hospital and returned to prison, her lawyers say
item.description: The convicted murderer was left in a critical condition after she survived two lethal injections.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘There is no secret agenda’: Nara Smith on home-making absolutely everything, raising four kids at 25 – and why she’s definitely not a tradwife
item.description: The model, actor and influencer is known for making her own frozen yoghurt, bubblegum or even toothpaste while dressed in immaculate haute couture. But she insists she is not who the internet thinks she is Nara Smith is…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Trump Accounts: Free money, but who gets a say?
item.description: Trump Accounts promise children a financial head start. Al Jazeera’s Emma Withrow spoke with one parent.

item.title: Ars Technica: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
item.description: Participants meditated inside an MRI tube, with and without psilocybin.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Kevin Roose Didn’t Use AI to Write His Book About AI
item.description: The author of The AGI Chronicles says his book “was written by a very tired, overworked, under-slept human being.”

item.title: WIRED Science: Humans Watched This Supernova Explode Nearly a Millennium Ago. Now You Can See It in High Definition
item.description: The new image isn’t just stunning—it may also provide clues about how this star survived its own explosion.

item.title: WIRED Business: I’m Still Convinced the iPod Was the Perfect Gadget
item.description: Apple’s original music player got many things right. Chief among them: It didn’t connect to the internet.

item.title: The New Yorker: What’s Driving the French Student Protests
item.description: A movement born in the Paris banlieues has mobilized young people against diminished school conditions and accumulating problems at home and beyond.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Are We Raising a Generation of Heteropessimists?
item.description: Friendship across genders makes the world feel less mysterious and hostile, but you can’t force it to happen.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Gowanopolis Rising
item.description: You can’t walk an inch in the Brooklyn neighborhood without running into a new luxury tower—or a toxic brownfield.

item.title: Fox59: Former funeral home director who overcharged families to live lavish lifestyle gets probation sentence for crimes
item.description: ANDERSON, Ind. — A former Madison County funeral director who overcharged customers tens of thousands of dollars in order to furnish her lavish lifestyle has avoided prison time thanks to accepting a plea deal. Adrianna…
